title: The global search PR queried MailAccount and MailRule with plain .objects.filter() behind only a model-level has_perm check, unlike the owner-aware get_objects_for_user_owner_aware() it used for tags and correspondents, so users see other users' mail accounts and rules.

vulnerable_findings.explanation: The PR relocates SearchResultSerializer from src/documents/views.py to src/documents/serialisers.py and, in doing so, drops the PassUserMixin base class. The base version was `class SearchResultSerializer(DocumentSerializer, PassUserMixin)`; the new version is `class SearchResultSerializer(DocumentSerializer)`. PassUserMixin (src/documents/views.py:213-224) is what injects `user=self.request.user`

findings.explanation: The new GlobalSearchView returns MailRule and MailAccount objects (both subclasses of ModelWithOwner, i.e. owner-scoped objects) using a plain `MailRule.objects.filter(...)` / `MailAccount.objects.filter(...)` queryset, gated only by the global `paperless_mail.view_mailrule` / `paperless_mail.view_mailaccount` permission. Unlike documents, tags, correspondents, document types and storage paths — which are filtered through `get_objects_for_user_owner_aware` — these owner-aware objects are not restricted to the requester's owned/unowned/permissioned set. Per the policy, global permissions only determine whether a user can access the area, while individual objects still have object-level permissions. A user with the global view permission can therefore enumerate and view the names of mail rules/accounts owned by other users, an IDOR-style exposure of objects the requester does not own.

evidence.content:
def get_objects_for_user_owner_aware(user, perms, Model) -> QuerySet:
    objects_owned = Model.objects.filter(owner=user)
    objects_unowned = Model.objects.filter(owner__isnull=True)
    objects_with_perms = get_objects_for_user(user=user, perms=perms, klass=Model, accept_global_perms=False)
    return objects_owned | objects_unowned | objects_with_perms

Global permissions define what areas of the app and API endpoints the user can access. For example, they determine if a user can create, edit, delete or view _any_ documents, but individual documents themselves still have "object-level" permissions.

findings.suggested_fix: Filter mail_rules and mail_accounts through get_objects_for_user_owner_aware(request.user, "view_mailrule"/"view_mailaccount", MailRule/MailAccount) so only objects the requester owns, that are unowned, or that they have explicit object-level permission to view are returned.

findings.explanation: The PR relocates SearchResultSerializer from src/documents/views.py to src/documents/serialisers.py and, in doing so, drops the PassUserMixin base class. The base version was `class SearchResultSerializer(DocumentSerializer, PassUserMixin)`; the new version is `class SearchResultSerializer(DocumentSerializer)`. PassUserMixin (src/documents/views.py:213-224) is what injects `user=self.request.user` into the serializer via get_serializer. DocumentSerializer's to_representation (and the permission fields it exposes, e.g. user_can_change / is_shared_by_requester at serialisers.py:790-792) rely on that user to compute object-level permissions. The new to_representation (serialisers.py:800-824) fetches the full Document by user-controlled id (`Document.objects...get(id=instance["id"])`) and serializes it without the user context, so the object-level permission check that the policy requires (docs/api.md: 'the user must be the object owner or a superuser'; docs/usage.md: 'individual documents themselves still have object-level permissions') is no longer applied. This newly exposes the relocated serializer to returning documents the requester is not permitted to view.
